In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the network dynamics is chaotic and that the fluctuations are fractal.

the TCP dynamics is a very rich one, that is not well captured by the classical TCP models, and that is extremely sensitive to the network topology, to the buffer size, to the number of TCP flows, to the synchronization level and to the RTT distribution.
synchronization in TCP controlled networks is a complex phenomenon, whose consequences on the network performance and on the fairness of the flows can be quite unexpected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamics of TCP controlled flows in a large scale network is very complex, and that synchronization effects are crucial to understand it.
TCP's performance is extremely sensitive to the network parameters, and that the network as a system has to be analyzed as a whole, and cannot be decomposed into its components.
we have shown that the TCP dynamics can be understood as a billiard dynamics in high dimension, that the billiard dynamics is chaotic and that it exhibits fractal fluctuations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
synchronization is not an artifact of simulations, but that it is a very real and unavoidable phenomenon in the real world.
, in the presence of a large population of flows, a network can exhibit a complex dynamics that is due to the network and not to individual flows.
, for a large population of flows sharing a network, synchronization effects are very strong.
